claim: Small GTPases act as molecular switches, being turned on in their active GTP form by GEFs and turned off in the GDP form by GAPs.
source: These small proteins act as molecular switches, being turned on in their active GTP form by a large variety of guanine exchange factors (GEFs) and turned off in the GDP form by GTPase activating proteins (GAPs) (Cherfils and Zeghouf, 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites established knowledge about GTPase regulation.

claim: Early experiments expressing GTPases in their active forms led to the canonical picture in which Rac1 and Cdc42 promote protrusion while RhoA promotes retraction.
source: Early experiments expressing these GTPases in their active forms (Hall, 1998) led to the canonical picture in which Rac1 and Cdc42 promotes protrusion, with the presence of ruffles and filopodia, while RhoA promotes retraction, as testified by cell rounding and actomyosin contractility.
evidence: The manuscript cites established knowledge about GTPase functions.

claim: RhoA has been proposed to be responsible for both protrusion and retraction depending on the cellular context.
source: This is especially true for RhoA, since it has been proposed to be responsible for both protrusion and retraction depending on the cellular context (Machacek et al., 2009; Pertz et al., 2006; Worthylake et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work showing context-dependent RhoA function.

claim: Optogenetic approaches to control Rac1 and Cdc42 have shown that recruitment of minimal GEF activating domains causally induces cell protrusions.
source: For example, we and others have shown that for Rac1 and Cdc42, despite of a complex cross-activation, the recruitment at the plasma membrane of minimal GEF activating domains causally induce cell protrusions (de Beco et al., 2018) and migration led by the front (Vaidžiulytė et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior optogenetic work on Rac1 and Cdc42.

claim: Optogenetic approaches to control RhoA have all shown a causal induction of cell retraction.
source: Along the same line, optogenetic approaches to control RhoA, reviewed in Chandrasekar et al., 2023 and de Seze et al., 2023, have all shown a causal induction of cell retraction.
